day_shape: 65 items: Iran International reports UK PM Burnham gaming out renewed US strikes on Iran and a possible Hormuz confrontation, IDF names three PIJ operatives killed in Gaza City strike disputed as aid workers, CENTCOM denies IRGC F-16 claim, heavy Basij/martyr messaging from Tehran, nothing from UK Parliament or OFAC.

threads.label: UK and US brace for renewed Iran strikes
threads.summary: Iran International, citing Bloomberg, reported UK PM Andy Burnham and ministers are preparing for possible renewed US strikes on Iran and economic fallout, while Iran International also said Tehran signalled it would not back down against a US maritime buildup near Hormuz. Jerusalem Post commentary flagged Netanyahu's reported push for a short air campaign and analyst Yaakov Katz pointing to refineries and power plants as potential third-strike targets.

threads.label: CENTCOM rebuts IRGC F-16 claim
threads.summary: CENTCOM publicly denied an IRGC claim that it had damaged a US F-16 and forced an emergency landing, saying no US fighter was attacked. IRIB separately attributed an explosion heard in Bandar Abbas to disposal of ammunition left from "the American-Zionist enemy."

threads.label: Gaza City strike on disputed 'aid' vehicle
threads.summary: The IDF said it struck three Palestinian Islamic Jihad operatives in a vehicle in Tel al-Hawa, Gaza City, naming engineering platoon commander Ahmed Badran Nimr Suweifri and two others, and rejecting claims they were aid workers. Reuters witnesses and World Central Kitchen documents were cited in early reports; WCK denied any link to the vehicle.

threads.label: Hamas disarmament framework stalls
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported the Board of Peace framework to disarm Hamas has made little progress, with BoP senior adviser Josh Greenbaum saying Israel is increasingly viewed internationally as the party holding things up and criticism turning toward Netanyahu. Former Mossad official Oded Ailam warned Hamas must be prevented from becoming "Gaza's Hezbollah."

threads.label: Lebanon independence messaging from US and IDF
threads.summary: Secretary Rubio issued a statement marking Lebanon's 83rd independence anniversary, reaffirming US support for a fully sovereign Lebanon. IDF Arabic spokesperson Avichay Adraee posted a series of Arabic-language messages to Lebanese audiences urging removal of Iranian influence, while Jerusalem Post cited a warning from Sarit Zehavi against mistaking Hezbollah's current restraint for lasting change.

threads.label: Iran domestic unrest, executions and deaths
threads.summary: Iran International reported truck drivers striking across multiple cities over freight rates and costs, two political prisoners moved to solitary confinement on security charges after murder death sentences were overturned, three deaths and 66 poisonings from counterfeit alcohol in Neyshabur, and a Sharif University student's suicide. The outlet also carried a witness account of January's Rasht protest crackdown and a family source alleging a 16-year-old girl was thrown from a fifth-floor window by her father.

threads.label: Khamenei and Basig messaging cycle
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted a "Countdown" message reiterating the Supreme Leader's prediction that Israel will not exist 25 years from a decade-old statement, alongside Vahid Khorasani memorial imagery. Defa Press and IRIB ran heavy Basij 48th-anniversary coverage, a Jaan-Feda caravan dispatch to Persian Gulf islands, farewell rites for "security defender" Ali Azad, and a claim by the Star of Persian Gulf Oil CEO that Iran is near self-sufficiency in petrol and diesel.

A gas pipeline explosion in the Ward area of Alabama state sent massive flames into the sky and smoke and fire were visible from several kilometres away. Emergency and fire response groups were present at the incident scene. The cause of the explosion is still unknown and no reports of casualties have been released so far. Authorities have asked residents of surrounding areas to exercise caution and avoid approaching the incident scene.

events.summary_en: One of the most powerful messages I sent to the Lebanese last year which remains present especially on Lebanon's independence anniversary: O heirs of Cadmus who taught the world the alphabet, O descendants of Gibran Khalil Gibran who sang of love and freedom, O those who chanted with Fairuz the celestial ambassador songs of glory and dignity... The time has come for Lebanon to return to its people, free, sovereign, independent and a beacon of civilisation as it has always been. Avichay Adraee. Special: O noble Lebanese people, O heirs of Cadmus who taught the world the alphabet, O descendants of Gibran Khalil Gibran who sang of love and freedom, O those who chanted with Fairuz the celestial ambassador songs of glory and dignity... I address you today with a heart that understands the value of your immortal civilisation.

events.title_en: I hope the Lebanese feels optimistic because history has given him a rare opportunity to build his nation so it is free as his thought and sovereign as its history and independent as its dream.
events.summary_en:
I hope the Lebanese feels optimistic because history has given him a rare opportunity to build his nation so it is free as his thought and sovereign as its history and independent as its dream.
Fate has willed Lebanon to become a theatre of conflicts but the decision today is in the hands of the Lebanese.
And as Lady Majida El Roumi sang to Beirut: 'Rise from under the rubble', we say: Rise from under the ashes of incitement and hypocrisy. Shake from your shoulders the illusions of manufactured enmity and build for your nation a towering edifice that future generations will be proud of. Ghassan Charbel. What does the Lebanese feel on Lebanon's independence anniversary?
